title: Consolidated SSO/KMS/RBAC Acceptance & Scope-change Checklist for Private Deploys
creator: Maya Patel
description: This ticket consolidates scope clarifications, PRD acceptance criteria, and an auditable sign-off checklist covering SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC role templates, audit logging schema & retention, and KMS/HSM operational controls for Private and VPC customer deployments. The intent is to: 1) lock requirements for the Private GA gating checklist, 2) document edge-case behavior and rollback criteria for emergency key rotation / SSO failover, and 3) provide deterministic acceptance tests that QA, Security, and Solutions Engineering can run during pilot onboarding. This PRD addendum responds to recent scope changes raised by Sales and Solutions: customer-managed HSM variants, delegated operator flows, and 3rd-party SAML IdP federation with nonstandard assertion mappings.
acceptance_criteria: SSO: SAML and OIDC federation can be configured via Console and via terraform template; SAML metadata upload and IdP-initiated flows validated with two federated IdPs (Okta + AzureAD)
SSO: Assertion attributes mapping supports at least two configurable mappings (email->principal, email+org->principal) and documented behavior for missing attributes
RBAC: Default role templates provided (Admin, Operator, ReadOnly, Billing) and least-privilege JSON policy examples for customer-managed operators
RBAC: Cross-tenant operator delegation proof: demo onboarding where a delegated operator can perform node maintenance without access to customer data or keys

Audit logs: Event schema v2 published (combined audit & telemetry) including fields for actor_type, actor_id, session_id, resource_type, action, success, request_id; retention configurable per-tenant with defaults (365 days for enterprise, 90 days for standard)
KMS/HSM: Customer-managed key import, wrap/unwrap APIs, and key rotation orchestration tested with AWS KMS + external HSM (YubiHSM / PKCS#11 provider) in a staging airgap
KMS: Emergency rotation path documented and automated so CRL-like fallback achieves 1-hour max service disruption across a dedicated pool
Operational: Console surfaces token-level cost and key-use dashboard with per-key access logs for the last 30 days
Integration tests: End-to-end tests that exercise SSO login, RBAC permission checks, audit event emission, and decrypt/sign operations complete in CI with deterministic fixtures
Compliance: Security approves the runbook and artifacts; Legal signs off on data residency and retention language

QA_plan: Create deterministic CI fixtures for SAML assertions with missing optional attributes to validate fallback mappings
Simulate delegated operator actions and assert no access to kms:Decrypt or key material exports
Run long-tail log ingestion test (10k events/hour) to validate audit pipeline and retention enforcement
Perform chaos test: simulate primary KMS key compromise and run emergency rotation choreography in staging; measure RTO and RPO
Onboarding smoke test: step-by-step playbook to validate console workflows, API templates, and terraform examples
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): feature behind feature-flag, internal dogfood orgs only
Phase 1 (pilot): invite 3 enterprise customers for private deploy pilots with dedicated support and runbook validation
Phase 2 (opt-in GA): open to customers on request with signed security questionnaire and onboarding window
Phase 3 (GA): public release with docs, terraform modules, and SOC2-lite guidance
Rollback criteria: failed pilot > 2 critical security defects OR emergency rotation RTO > 1 hour -> revert to previous runtime and pause new private deploys
notes: Sales requested support for IdP assertion customization for three strategic customers; we added a mapping template to reduce per-customer engineering work
We opted not to ship full custom policy language in v1 due to support load; revisit in Q3 after pilot feedback
Edge-case: some legacy IdPs send 'nameIdentifier' only; acceptance tests include this and document required normalization
Operational requirement: customer operators must authenticate through delegated SSO identity; operator short-lived certs rotate every 12 hours
Known risk: airgapped HSM providers vary in PKCS#11 behaviors; document expected provider compatibility matrix
